claim: Section 1: "(0.75–1.0 full-time on quotes, 40–60% recovered)"; Section 2: "(1.5 full-time reps, 50–60% of inquiries automatable, 14–34% gain)"; Section 3: "(10–20 hours a week on catalog and listing admin, 50–70% recovered)"
problem: These are staff-allocation assumptions, not public facts. No source states how many FTE cover quotes, inquiries or catalog admin; the company only says it has 'over 20 employees'. Written unhedged inside the Impact line, they read as known internal staffing - i.e. implied insider knowledge - and they carry the entire dollar range. (The arithmetic is correct: 1,560-2,080 hrs x 40-60% = 620-1,250; 3,120 hrs x 50-60% x 14-34% = 218-636; 520-1,040 hrs x 50-70% = 260-728. All three dollar totals reproduce at $27.81/hr and $28.69/hr.)
fix: Mark the inputs as assumptions, e.g. "Impact (our estimate): assuming roughly one to two people handle quotes part-time...", so the FTE/hour split is visibly an assumption rather than knowledge of their staffing.

claim: Sources: "O*NET NJ wages, order clerk (basis of $27.81/hour = $46,270 x 1.25 / 2,080; wage year not stated on the page)" and the identical parenthetical for the customer service rep page
problem: Contradicted by the pages themselves: both state "Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data" (site updated October 6, 2026). The audit asserts no wage year is given, which the client can check in one click. The $46,270 and $47,740 medians are correct.
fix: Replace with "2025 BLS OEWS wage data (NJ median) via O*NET" and delete the "wage year not stated" clause.

claim: Section 2, "Happening now": "Public ratings split by platform (4.6 stars over 429 reviews on Birdeye, 2.5 over 21 on Yelp excerpts), with packaging and order resolution the recurring complaints."
problem: The ratings are correct, but the complaint theme is attached to the ratings generally when it comes only from the syndicated Yelp sample: 21 reviews, visible excerpts dated 2017-2020, three mentioning packaging and one reporting an unresolved order. 'Recurring' for order resolution rests on a single review, so the sentence overstates the pattern and its age.
fix: Attribute and soften: "...2.5 over 21 on Yelp excerpts, where the few complaint reviews cite packaging and, in one case, an unresolved order."

claim: Section 2 impact basis: "14–34% gain", sourced to "NBER Working Paper 31161"
problem: The 14% average and 34% novice figures are confirmed, but the audit omits the setting: 5,179 agents at a Fortune 500 software vendor's support desk. As written the band looks measured for a 20-person distributor, and the 34% upper bound applies only to novice/low-skilled agents.
fix: Add a short parenthetical: "(measured on a large software vendor's support desk; the 34% applies to novice agents, so transfer to your team is our inference)".

problem: Correctly computed, but the underlying analysis.json states $18,000–$34,000 for the same workflow. Two different headline ranges for one opportunity is a credibility risk if both documents are read.
fix: Use the audit's computed range ($17,300-$34,700) in both documents.
